Frustrate

/frə-STRĀT/ — stress on second syllable, rhymes with gate · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To frustrate someone is to block them from getting what they want or expect, leaving them annoyed and disappointed.

The constant pop-up ads frustrate anyone trying to read the article.

Worked Example

During the championship soccer match, the referee called back a goal the team had just scored for a missed offside call, frustrating the entire team who thought they had won.

Frustrate captures exactly what happens: the team is actively blocked from their goal (the scored point) and left annoyed and disappointed. A milder word like 'disappoint' would miss the sense that they were prevented from what they expected.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

annoy: to irritate someone in small ways

disappoint: to fail to meet someone's hopes

thwart: to block a plan from succeeding

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

assist: to help someone reach their goal

satisfy: to fulfill someone's wants or expectations

Where it sits · how completely someone's goals get blocked — disappoint → irritate → exasperate → frustrate

disappoint vs. frustrate: Disappoint is weaker than frustrate: to disappoint is to let someone's hopes down once, while to frustrate is to actively block them from what they want.

irritate vs. frustrate: Irritate is weaker than frustrate; small things irritate you in passing, but to frustrate someone is to keep thwarting their efforts until they feel defeated.

exasperate vs. frustrate: Exasperate is strong, but frustrate caps this scale: to exasperate is to push annoyance to its limit, while to frustrate adds the deeper sting of having your goals completely blocked.

Build the Word

The pieces

Root — frustra

Root — frustra: in vain, uselessly (Latin)

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: verb-forming: to make or cause (Latin (-atus))

Put it together

Put it together: Frustrate literally means 'to make (someone's efforts) be in vain.' When pop-up ads frustrate a reader, they render every attempt useless — blocking people from what they want and leaving them annoyed and disappointed.

Use the root in a new word: frustration

Use the root in a new word: frustration: Her frustration grew each time the website crashed — frustration is the feeling left behind whenever something frustrates your plans, making all your effort feel 'in vain.'

Word Building

Word Choice

neutral

Frustrate goes beyond mere annoyance or disappointment — it specifically means being blocked from what you want or expect, then left annoyed and disappointed. Use annoyed for mild irritation; use frustrated when someone is actively prevented from reaching a goal.
